summary: The audit checks the Philosophy and Religious Studies core courses, the Philosophy breadth areas (each letter graded, at least 3 units, C- or better), two RELIGST 100-289 courses and RELIGST 290, WIM, a capstone in either department, and 60 units in all: at least 16 units of Philosophy, 20 units of Religious Studies, and 20 units numbered 100 or above across the two, with at most 5 of the additional (depth) units in each department below 100. At most 10 units graded S or CR count. Checked by hand: three seminars (the Bulletin does not say which), and the honors applications and theses. Left: the program summary says 20 units in each department, but the Philosophy depth text says 16 Philosophy units, and the audit uses 16.

AtzcPr0U.why: "The Honors Thesis is a 40-80 page research paper ... Applicants for honors must have a grade point average (GPA) of 3.5 in Religious Studies courses, and at least 3.2 overall ... Theses earning a grade of 'B+' or above receive honors." The courses are the Religious Studies capstone's; the application, GPA and thesis are checked by hand.
